coaching.summary: The decision is well-structured with three options and clear time/budget constraints, but several important causal pathways and risks are missing, which could leave the reasoning incomplete before analysis begins.

strengthen_items.label: Add a data quality or integration failure risk for the build option
strengthen_items.detail: A four-engineer team building a CDP in-house faces significant risk of incomplete data pipeline coverage or integration gaps that could undermine platform capability even if delivery is on time — this pathway is currently absent.

strengthen_items.label: Surface the opportunity cost of engineering capacity being consumed
strengthen_items.detail: Engineering capacity consumed by build already appears as a factor, but its downstream effect on other product work is not captured — adding this connection would make the true cost of the build option visible.

strengthen_items.label: Clarify what the status quo option means for the fiscal year goal
strengthen_items.detail: The status quo option flows into the same factors as the other options, but its specific consequence — missing the fiscal year deadline — is not explicitly linked to the goal, which may understate the cost of deferral.

strengthen_items.label: Distinguish vendor lock-in risk as specific to the buy option
strengthen_items.detail: Vendor lock-in and renewal cost escalation currently flows from total cost of implementation, which is shared across all options — making it explicit that this risk is asymmetrically tied to the buy option would sharpen the comparison.

elements_considered_but_excluded: Team skill gap / learning curve — relevant to build but no existing factor to attach it to without adding a new node
Stakeholder adoption / change management — important for CDP success but outside the current scope of the brief
Contract negotiation flexibility — relevant to buy option but not mentioned in the brief

bias_signals.detail: The brief anchors cost framing around '180k GBP annual contract' for the buy option, which may cause the in-house build cost to be evaluated relative to that figure rather than on its own full-cost basis.
The brief states the build can be done with 'our existing four-engineer data team' without acknowledging capacity limits or skill gaps, implying higher certainty of delivery than may be warranted.
The brief frames the choice as build vs. buy vs. defer, but the 'nine months' and '250k GBP' constraints are treated as fixed without exploring whether either could be negotiated or phased.
